title: Politics of performance replaced policy paralysis during PM Modi's rule: Amit Shah
excerpt: Vijayawada (Andhra Pradesh), Nov 16: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday said politics of performance replaced policy paralysis of earlier times during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's rule since 2014. He was speaking at an event in this city where Ramoji Excellence Awards instituted in memory of veteran journalist Ch Ramoji Rao were presented on the occasion of his birth anniversary. The awards were instituted by the Ramoji Group. Recalling the stellar contributions of Ramoji Rao, Shah said the former's contributions in journalism can only be compared with that of veteran Ramnath Goenka. "Ramoji Rao fought for values. He established values," Shah added. On the Modi-led NDA government, which is into its third term since 2014, Shah referred to the strides made in national security and economic progress. "During Modi rule, politics of performance and policy-based development took the place of policy paralysis which used to be discussed earlier," he said. The union minister said abolition of Article 370, ending five decades-old Naxalism, ensuring national security and economic progress were among the good work carried out under the Modi regime. While the development forecast of many countries has declined amid ongoing wars, the Moody's Ratings raised India's growth forecast from 6.5 per cent to 7 per cent, he said. While exports stood at USD 863 billion in 2025-26, the target for 2026-27 is USD one trillion, he said, expressing confidence of achieving it. India has emerged as the second largest producer of steel in the world and produces more steel than the combined production of the US and Japan, he said. He said that according to a World Bank report, 50 crore Indians have emerged out of poverty during PM Modi's 12 years in office. Patting Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu, Shah said the southern state was making rapid strides in progress under the CM's leadership. Recalling his meeting with Naidu at PM Modi's swearing in ceremony (2024), Shah said though he congratulated the former on his election victory, he had doubts about Andhra's progress as it was a revenue deficit state. "I am a student of development statistics of all states across the country. I am closely looking at the statistics of Chandrababu ji's second term. I can tell you that Andhra Pradesh would be the most developed state in the country in the coming 10 years. Nobody needs to have doubts about this," Shah said. The establishment of Google's USD 15 billion AI hub in Visakhapatnam is a matter of pride not only for Andhra Pradesh but for the people of entire India. PM Modi recently inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport in Visakhapatnam, and on the same day, foundation stones were laid for projects worth Rs 18,000 crore. A closer look at all these initiatives reveals that Naidu has brought investments worth Rs 30 lakh crore to Andhra Pradesh in two and a half years, the Home minister said. Heaping praises on Ramoji Rao, Shah said many individuals become institutions through their lifetime of work, and the institutions they founded continue to inspire the nation. The veteran journalist is one such extraordinary personality, Shah opined. Ramoji Rao was very clear about every problem facing the country and their solutions, and had strong opinions, which he had the courage to express openly. He said Ramoji Rao remains a role model for youth in many fields, including agriculture, education, filmmaking, and media. Shah said that when we look at the owners of today's newspapers and news channels, and their business objectives and profits, the magnitude of Ramoji Rao's personality can be understood. Ramoji Rao spent two major periods of his life struggling. Despite significant financial losses and numerous hardships, he maintained his news channel's impartiality and maintained a true fourth pillar of democracy, Shah stated. He further said Ramoji Rao also contributed to the film industry. Without the Ramoji Film City in Hyderabad, a film industry in any language is unimaginable. Speaking on the occasion, CM Naidu announced that the birth anniversary of Ramoji Rao would be observed as a state festival in recognition of his services. Despite being born in a remote village, Rao strived for perfection in every endeavour, Naidu said, noting that public interest, credibility and an uncompromising attitude formed his core values. Naidu said Ramoji Rao had suggested naming Andhra Pradesh's capital Amaravati, following the bifurcation which led to the existence of Telangana, after extensive research. The CM said Rao's family had donated Rs 10 crore for the greenfield capital city, and also extended financial aid to the Telugu states during covid-19 pandemic. Praising Rao's exploits in a plethora of realms, Naidu observed that he had always upheld ethics. Though the veteran had faced many challenges and political plots in his lifetime, he had never bowed down his head to anybody, Naidu said about Rao. For four decades, dictators had "conspired" against him, Naidu said. During his last days, the CM alleged that a bedridden Rao was troubled and those videos were made viral. He said that Rao is the pride of the Telugu community and an inspiration for generations. Rao's organizations are assets for the Telugu community, Naidu said and called on youth to draw inspiration from him. The awardees are Rajasekhar Raju under category of rural development and agriculture, V Rukmini Rao (women's rights), M Suchitra (journalism), Arjun Arunachalam (science & technology), Jema J Edcherry (medical & healthcare), Devendra Kumar Gupta (service to mankind), Maitreyi Jijhkar (education) and Ganesh Barayya (youth icon), among others. Andhra Governor Abdul Nazeer, Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan, Union ministers Kishan Reddy, K Ram Mohan Naidu and Bh Srinivasa Varma and Ramoji Group CMD Ch Kiron attended the event.

title: How Venkat Ramana Turned Mumbai's ValuePitch Into a Background-Verification Platform Searching 95 Crore Legal Records
excerpt: A background check can become complicated when court records are scattered across jurisdictions and a person's name appears differently in different documents. Finding a relevant case is only part of the challenge; establishing whether it belongs to the person being checked is equally important. Name variations, initials, and incomplete details can make matching difficult, particularly when several people share similar names. Without checking case details, dates and locations, a relevant record may be missed or wrongly attributed to someone. Mumbai-headquartered ValuePitch has built its business around making these searches faster and more accessible. It brings together court judgments, case-status information, and other legal documents, allowing organisations to search a database containing 95 crore records. The company was not originally built as a background-verification business. It began with digital marketing services and gradually moved into legal data and identity matching. Its founder and Chief Executive Officer, Venkat Ramana, says that the shift came from applying the company's information-gathering capabilities to a different problem. “We have around 15 crore judgments and 80 crore other legal documents, which include orders and case-status records. These come from district courts, high courts, the Supreme Court, and tribunals,” Venkat, founder of ValuePitch, tells Startup Pedia in an exclusive interview. The platform processes nearly 20 lakh searches a month, while the company puts its annual search volume at about 2 crore, a rounded figure. Its customers use the technology for employee verification, borrower checks, and other due-diligence requirements. Venkat’s Journey to ValuePitch Before building ValuePitch, Venkat served as Head of India Operations at Movers.com from 2002 to 2004 in Telangana. He then became Director of Delivery at Pinstorm, beginning his Mumbai career, before serving as a founder advisor at Recommendly. From 2017 to 2021, he also founded and led Ideastorm.in, a Mumbai-based community meetup group hosting weekly brainstorming, problem-solving, and product ideation sessions. For ValuePitch, he says, “The company began in 2006 as ValuePitch IT Interactive Services Pvt Ltd, an IT services company whose services were in digital marketing. The current company, ValuePitch eTechnologies Pvt Ltd, was set up in 2010.” One of its early offerings was an online reputation-monitoring product launched in 2007. It helped businesses track discussions about their brands across internet forums when social media platforms were yet to become the dominant channels for online conversations. That work introduced the company to a new kind of business problem: how to collect information from different sources and turn it into something organisations could act on. The journey and challenges of building ValuePitch In 2008, ValuePitch began working with a leading private-sector bank on an ATM-related matter. This was the time of the global financial crisis. Major Indian private-sector banks faced waves of panic and withdrawal queues triggered by rumors circulating via SMS, emails, and online forums about the bank's financial health and cash availability at ATMs. The company helped monitor online discussions and supplied information to a control centre where teams could respond to customer concerns. Venkat recalls the scale of the situation, “There was a run on the bank's ATMs all over. So, we were the ones helping the bank with monitoring what was happening in the forums.” This experience gradually led the company towards legal data and identity matching, opening up a new application for its information-gathering capabilities. “ValuePitch began developing identity-matching capabilities in 2013, and one of India's largest IT services companies became its first background-verification client in 2014,” Venkat recalls. The December 2014 Uber incident in Delhi, the kidnapping and sexual assault of a 25-year-old female passenger by an Uber driver, also brought greater attention to background verification in the commercial transportation sector. “The Uber incident made the market understand the importance of quality background checks. Demand for rigorous checks grew after it,” Venkat says. By 2017, ValuePitch had signed up around 100 value-added partners, expanding the reach of its background-verification services. The company identified two persistent gaps in India's verification process. First, criminal-record checks could be restricted to individual police-station jurisdictions. A check in one city might not reveal a case registered elsewhere, even when the person had moved between locations. “What was clear was the gap: the criminal check was being conducted at the police station level. But what about the police station next door or the police station where I come from?”, Venkat says. The second challenge involved matching identities across inconsistent records. Names, addresses, fathers' names, and dates of birth can be entered in different formats. Spelling variations and regional-language scripts add further complications. To solve this issue, Venkat said ValuePitch had developed a common search algorithm to account for spelling variations and names written in regional languages, including Telugu, Bengali, Marathi, and Malayalam. He separately clarified that Aadhaar numbers do not appear in court records, meaning those records cannot be searched using Aadhaar numbers. “We sorted and unified all of that into a common search algorithm. One part was creating an all-India search, and the second was solving the identity-matching problem itself,” he says. ValuePitch: Searching 95 crore legal records ValuePitch’s database comprises approximately 15 crore judgments and 80 crore other legal documents, including orders and case-status records. The company extracts identities from court documents and maps them against case details, dates, and locations. It then indexes the information in different forms and converts the records into a search-friendly format to improve retrieval speed and accuracy. “All this data is converted to be search-friendly from an accuracy and speed point of view. When a search comes to our system from the client, it can retrieve within a second from these 95 crore records,” Venkat says. He says its information is updated daily and its reported accuracy exceeds 99%. “[But] two gaps remain. One is error: about 1% false positives and around 1 in 1,00,000 misses. The other is that a lot of court data is not yet digitised,” he explains. There are also cases that may not appear in the database, including certain matters involving women, children, minors, and sensitive proceedings. As a result, a ‘no record found’ result does not always mean that no case exists; the relevant record may simply be absent from the database. “The candidate or the client can escalate a result to us. We review the facts and the latest legal status of the case, and correct the report on merits. We do not recommend a hiring or lending decision; we only flag the underlying issue. We recommend that the client confirm it or discuss it with the candidate. For serious cases, we offer on-the-ground confirmation from multiple sources,” Venkat says. ValuePitch complies with applicable laws and is ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certified. Venkat also says the company is ready for the Digital Personal Data Protection framework. Its product portfolio includes Verify24x7, Instacheck, Related Party Search, and Court Checker. The company also offers Know Your Founder (KYF), a product for investors assessing founders before making an investment. “What we do is put together a 360-degree profile,” Venkat says of KYF. The report can cover identity, employment, financial stress, challans, criminal history, and litigation. “KYF is fully live. Founders give consent digitally before their information is included in a report,” he explains. How ValuePitch makes money and measures growth An important distinction in ValuePitch's model is the difference between a search and a completed verification. “A search works like a Google search: it returns the top 50 possible matches. A completed check is that result taken further, at one of several levels: machine-filtered, manually filtered, or confirmed and certified by a lawyer. Price depends on the scope and volume of checks,” Venkat explains. Venkat says a conventional verification can take around three days, while ValuePitch's process can take as little as four hours. He also says the cost of a verification has come down from approximately Rs 700-750 to under Rs 100. The company has around 400-500 direct clients, while its indirect reach through value-added partners is estimated to be approximately 10 times higher. Venkat says,“ValuePitch also provides Court Checker and Verify24x7 to over 1,00,000 individual police officials across India, free of charge since 2014. Users are verified through due process.” “The employee-verification segment contributes more than 60% of the company's revenue. Banks and non-banking financial companies account for around 25%,” he adds. Venkat describes ValuePitch as bootstrapped and profitable, with more than 70 employees. The company recorded average annual revenue of Rs 20 crore over the last three years. He clarified that this is recurring revenue and that its accounts are audited. What's next for ValuePitch ValuePitch is working to build on its existing business across employee verification, financial institutions, and government-related opportunities. Venkat said the company was involved in four state-government pilots, but declined to name the states while tender processes were pending. It has also been exploring CCTV-based video intelligence through NthEye, a project that remains in stealth mode until the end of 2026. Venkat confirmed that Rs 20 crore is the baseline for the company's 2027 revenue target. “In the 2027 calendar year, we're going to double the revenue with the existing pipeline that we have,” he concludes. FAQ Q. What does ValuePitch do? A. ValuePitch provides background verification and legal record search services to businesses, helping them assess employees, borrowers, and other identities. How many records does ValuePitch's platform search? Its database contains approximately 95 crore records, including 15 crore court judgments and 80 crore other legal documents. Who founded ValuePitch? Venkat Ramana founded ValuePitch in 2006 as an IT services company focused on digital marketing. It later expanded into legal data and background verification. What products does ValuePitch offer? ValuePitch offers Verify24x7, Instacheck, Related Party Search, and Court Checker. It also provides Know Your Founder (KYF), a product for investors to check founders.

title: Maharashtra To Launch India's First Statewide SO₂ Emissions Trading Scheme On November 17 To Tackle Industrial Air Pollution
excerpt: Maharashtra will launch India's first statewide sulphur dioxide emissions trading scheme on November 17 in Mumbai, the MPCB said. Under the initiative, industries can trade emission permits, rewarding facilities that cut pollution at lower costs. Developed with the Emissions Market Accelerator, the scheme aims to improve air quality for around 13 crore people across the state.
